items.title: Show HN: Tutor, a self-hosted LLM tutor that teaches you your books or docs
items.contentSnippet:
Reading does not always guarantee retention, especially for complex materials. So I created this tool which extracts the concepts and teach them back to you (and then test you as much as you need) so you can really learn the study material.
This is a local project (hosted option coming soon) and it works for EPUB, PDF books or online HTML pages.

I built Flopper to make it easier to compare GPUs and understand the tradeoffs for workloads for AI and beyond.

items.contentSnippet:
Open weight AI is like open source software. Users not only run the weights, but also modify the weights. It matters to develop training framework for local hardware.
The method to train large AI models on local hardware is generally called QLoRA (Low Rank Adaptation over Quantized base model). items.title: Show HN: A fullscreen Game of Life in which every board is a runnable program
items.contentSnippet:
Each tile is a Piet program that prints a word.
Each generation, every tile runs.
After, its label shows what it printed.
The original was a Piet program, compiled from Temper by a backend I wrote, playing Life on another Piet program:
3 hours, 1.27 billion steps. Generation 0 printed "Piet!".
